queer_characters.name: Ruby
queer_characters.notes: Ruby is one of the Gems (designed as non-binary women) and is in a romantic same-sex relationship with Sapphire; they had the first same-sex wedding in children's animation.

queer_characters.name: Sapphire
queer_characters.notes: Sapphire is a Gem (non-binary woman) in a romantic same-sex relationship with Ruby, culminating in an on-screen wedding.

queer_characters.name: Garnet
queer_characters.notes: Garnet is the romantic fusion of Ruby and Sapphire, embodying their same-sex relationship; leader of the Crystal Gems.

queer_characters.name: Stevonnie
queer_characters.notes: Fusion of Steven and Connie who explicitly uses they/them pronouns in the show.

queer_characters.name: Fluorite
queer_characters.notes: A six-Gem fusion described in the source as representing polyamorous relationships; Gems are non-binary women.

queer_characters.name: Pearl
queer_characters.notes: Pearl is a Gem (non-binary woman); an embrace between Rose and Pearl that was censored by Cartoon Network UK suggests romantic subtext, though the source does not explicitly confirm her orientation.
queer_characters.contest_notes: The source only mentions a removed embrace between Rose and Pearl framed as same-sex; her orientation is not explicitly stated in the provided text.

queer_characters.name: Amethyst
queer_characters.notes: Amethyst is one of the Crystal Gems, deliberately designed by Sugar as a genderless alien projecting a female form ('non-binary women').

queer_creators.name: Rebecca Sugar
queer_creators.notes: Sugar publicly identifies as a non-binary, bisexual woman and stated the show's LGBTQ themes drew on her own experience; first non-binary person to independently create a Cartoon Network show.

contributor_notes: Draft based solely on provided source. Ruby/Sapphire tagged 'queer'/'nonbinary' because the source describes Gems as 'non-binary women' in a same-sex relationship rather than using a specific label like lesbian; a maintainer may refine. Pearl marked contested as her orientation is only implied via the censored Rose/Pearl embrace. Homophobia trigger reflects in-narrative context and real-world censorship/banning described; consider whether real-world context belongs in trigger_warnings.
